chunks: And from him, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from al-'Ala' ibn Razin, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said:
I asked him about a man who misses the daytime prayer, he said: 'He makes it up if he wishes after Maghrib, and if he wishes, after 'Isha.'
ai.seo_question: When can a missed daytime prayer be made up according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the flexibility in making up missed daytime prayers (Dhuhr or 'Asr), allowing the believer to perform qada either after Maghrib or after 'Isha based on personal convenience. This ruling reflects the Shia juristic principle of ease (taysir) in worship, ensuring that missed obligations do not become a burden due to rigid timing constraints. It underscores the practical application of prayer continuity in daily life, emphasizing that the validity of qada is not strictly bound to the immediate window of the missed prayer's time.
